subject: Nanotechnology
title: Micro-Supercapacitors on Chip
description: A micro-lesson that makes Micro-Supercapacitors on Chip usable.

hook.text: A supercapacitor thinner than a human hair sits on a microchip — powering a sensor from its own tiny reservoir.

buildup.text: Interdigitated finger electrodes patterned by lithography maximize edge length in minimal area.

discovery.text: Carbon nanotube or graphene forests grown between the fingers provide huge surface area in microns of height.

twist.text: Electrolyte choices for on-chip use are limited — gel and solid electrolytes avoid leakage but have lower conductivity.

climax.text: Integrated micro-supercapacitors now pair with energy harvesters — self-powered IoT chips that never need batteries.

punchline.text: Shrink the supercapacitor onto the chip and the chip powers itself.

quiz.question: Why are micro-supercapacitors valuable for IoT devices?
options: They replace the processor on the chip
They store energy on-chip for burst power, enabling battery-free self-powered sensor nodes
They transmit data faster than conventional chips
